I've been on that. It's a jarring ride and a funicular railway. It climbs up the side of the mountain. I can see the mountain from my front windows, actually.

Mt. Washington is a rough mountain. It's often very rough conditions at the top. There's a wonderful story about how it got a road and railway. Basically, the legislature didn't think the guy would be able to do it, so they told him he could build it to the moon. But, he did build the train and road. He was pretty happy about this, but hasn't gone on to build it out to the moon - even though he has the right of way to do so.

The auto road is pretty sweet and a great drive when the sky's clear. In the winter, if it's not too bad, you can go up in special vans that have tracks. Warning, it's cold. People still die on the mountain, though that's a rarity. Getting lost may cost you the rescue fees. There was a heated debate about that, but a stupid climber pretty much sealed the deal.

Interesting side effect, parts of the road are so steep that you'll leak windshield washer fluid from your rear window - should you have an SUV. They prefer you drive it with a standard transmission and don't let you go up with an automatic unless it has a clearly indicated low gear. This is because you will need to use engine braking. Otherwise, your brakes will overheat and fail.

It's still a great drive. They give you a CD to listen to and a sticker to put on your car that says, "This car climbed Mt. Washington."
